title: Opinions and Feelings
description: Say what you think and how you feel — and disagree the Sanaa way, with a softener before the punch. The mafraj debate on light topics: qat, football, whose city has the better bread.
approach: GPA Phase 4 — the learner hears two friends disagree politely, sorts the softeners from the opinions, then argues a light topic with the AI.
unlock_condition: Give an opinion with أظن إنه, agree once and disagree once with a softener, judged natural by the AI
can_do: Give your opinion and agree or disagree politely
Say you like or hate something

grammar.title: أظن إنه… : the little إن that carries an opinion
grammar.explanation: Opinion verbs — أظن 'I think', أحس 'I feel', أعرف 'I know', قال 'he said' — link to the next sentence with إن, which takes a pronoun ending: إني، إنك، إنه، إنها، إنهم. أظن إنه غالي 'I think that it's expensive'. When the next word is a name or noun you can still say إن: أظن إن القات غالي. The إن is often dropped in fast speech, so you will hear أظن غالي too, but keep it when you are the one talking — it shows control. For 'in my opinion' use في رأيي; the softeners مع احترامي 'with respect' and معليش بس 'sorry, but' go in front of a disagreement.

examples.english: I think that it's very expensive
I feel the weather is colder today

examples.arabic: في رأيي، السلتة أحسن من المندي
examples.transliteration: fi raʾyi, is-salta aḥsan min il-mandi
examples.english: In my opinion, saltah is better than mandi
He said that he's coming in the afternoon

culture.title: Disagree, but land it softly
culture.note: Sanaa loves an argument — the afternoon qat session runs on them — but the form matters. Start with agreement even if you are about to disagree: عندك حق، بس… 'you're right, but…'. Say مع احترامي 'with respect' before contradicting an older man, and finish a heated point with بس هذا رأيي 'but that's just my opinion' so nobody loses. Safe topics: food, football, the price of qat, which region's mountains are prettier. Leave alone: politics, someone's tribe or region, and any family's private business. Feelings are stated freely among friends — أنا حانق 'I'm angry' is normal — but never about a host's food or house.

phrases.english: You're right, but in my opinion…

phrases.arabic: بس هذا رأيي، ما أفرضهش على أحد
phrases.transliteration: bass haadha raʾyi, maa afriḍhush ʿala aḥad
phrases.english: But that's my opinion, I don't force it on anyone

vocabulary.teaching_note: The safest opinion verb. ظ is the heavy dh: aẓunn. Followed by إن. You will also hear أحسب (very Sanaa) and أعتقد.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man with a finger on his temple and a thought bubble with a question mark.
vocabulary.video_hint: Opinion vlogs and street interviews; أظن at the start of an answer.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Fronts an opinion and makes it personal, which is polite. برأيي is the same. Ask back with ايش رأيك؟
vocabulary.image_scene: A woman with one hand on her chest and the other open, speaking calmly.

example.english: In my opinion, Adeni tea is nicer

vocabulary.video_hint: Debates on light topics; في رأيي before a claim.

vocabulary.teaching_note: A participle: أنا موافق 'I agree', موافقة for a woman, موافقين for us. ق is g. The one-word yes to a proposal.
vocabulary.image_scene: Two men shaking hands with nods, a thumbs-up from a third.

example.english: I agree with you a hundred percent

vocabulary.video_hint: Agreement in conversation; موافق with a nod.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The plain disagreement: مش before the participle. Soften it with معليش بس or عندك حق بس. مش موافقة for a woman.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man shaking his head with a raised palm, calm face.

example.arabic: معليش، بس أنا مش موافق على هذا
example.transliteration: maʿleesh, bass ana mish muwaafig ʿala haadha
example.english: Sorry, but I don't agree with this

vocabulary.video_hint: Debates; مش موافق right after a claim.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The everyday 'happy': مبسوط من الشغل 'happy with work'. فرحان is the bigger joy. Feminine مبسوطة.
vocabulary.image_scene: A young man grinning widely, arms wide, on a sunny rooftop.
vocabulary.video_hint: Reunions and good news; مبسوط said with a smile.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The Yemeni 'angry' — from حنق. حانق منك 'angry at you', حنقت 'I got angry', لا تحنق 'don't be angry'. زعلان is milder, more 'upset'.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man with furrowed brows and clenched fist, steam-style lines around his head.
vocabulary.video_hint: Comedy sketches with a fuming character; حانق / حنقت in the lines.

vocabulary.teaching_note: ق is g: zahgaan. زهقت 'I'm bored / fed up', ملّيت is the older Sanaa word. Feminine زهقانة.
vocabulary.image_scene: A teenager slumped on a cushion staring at a blank wall, phone dead.

example.english: I'm bored of the house, shall we go for a walk?

vocabulary.video_hint: Lockdown or lazy-day vlogs; زهقت said while sprawled out.

vocabulary.teaching_note: From هم 'worry' — the Yemeni series همي همك means 'my worry is your worry'. مهموم على 'worried about'. Also قلقان and خايف على.
vocabulary.image_scene: A woman looking at her phone with a hand on her cheek, night outside.

example.arabic: أنا مهموم على أخوي في الغربة
example.english: I'm worried about my brother abroad

vocabulary.video_hint: Emotional family vlogs; مهموم / همي in the narration.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Literally 'it pleases me', so the thing is the subject: يعجبني القات 'I like qat', تعجبني صنعاء 'I like Sanaa' (feminine). أحب is 'I love / I like' too.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man giving a delighted thumbs-up at a plate of saltah.

example.english: I like the cold in Sanaa

vocabulary.video_hint: Reviews; يعجبني / أعجبني about a dish or a place.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Strong but common: أكره الزحمة 'I hate traffic'. ما أحبش is the gentler 'I don't like'.
vocabulary.image_scene: A woman wrinkling her nose at a plate of something, pushing it away.

example.english: I hate the heat in Hodeidah

vocabulary.video_hint: Rants and reaction clips; أكره with an exaggerated face.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Both body and opinion: أحس بتعب 'I feel tired', أحس إنه غلط 'I feel it's wrong'. Doubled s at the end.
vocabulary.image_scene: A woman with a hand on her forehead and a thought bubble with a thermometer.

example.english: I feel lunch was too much

vocabulary.video_hint: Any first-person reaction; أحس before a feeling.

vocabulary.teaching_note: ايش رأيك؟ 'what do you think?' is the invitation to every debate. رأيي 'my opinion', آراء 'opinions'.
vocabulary.image_scene: A speech bubble with a lightbulb inside, held up like a sign.

example.english: What's your opinion of the new restaurant?

vocabulary.video_hint: Hosts asking ايش رأيكم؟ to the audience.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Signals a blunt opinion is coming — and softens it at the same time. بصراحة، ما عجبنيش 'frankly, I didn't like it'.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man leaning in with an open hand, eyebrows up, about to speak plainly.

example.english: Frankly, I didn't like the film

vocabulary.video_hint: Reviews and reactions; بصراحة before the verdict.

vocabulary.teaching_note: هذا غلط 'this is wrong', أنت غلطان 'you're mistaken'. Used for facts and behaviour alike; the noun 'a mistake' is غلطة.
vocabulary.image_scene: A large red cross over a maths sum on a blackboard.

example.english: The answer is wrong, try again

vocabulary.video_hint: Quiz shows and corrections; غلط with a buzzer.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The opposite of غلط and also the tag 'right?': غالي، صح؟ Double the ḥ. صحيح is the longer form.
vocabulary.image_scene: A big green tick on a whiteboard, a teacher nodding.
vocabulary.video_hint: Confirmation tags at the end of sentences; صح؟

vocabulary.teaching_note: The softener before every disagreement: عندك حق، بس… To a woman عندش حق (Sanaa -ish). ق is g: ḥagg.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man nodding with a hand raised in concession to a friend.

example.arabic: عندك حق، بس القات غالي قوي
example.transliteration: ʿindak ḥagg, bass il-gaat ghaali gawi
example.english: You're right, but qat is really expensive

vocabulary.video_hint: Debates; عندك حق conceded before a بس.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Flips a claim: مش غالي، بالعكس، رخيص 'not expensive — the opposite, cheap'. Very common in friendly argument.
vocabulary.image_scene: Two arrows pointing opposite ways, a woman pointing the other way.

example.english: I wasn't bored, on the contrary, I enjoyed myself

vocabulary.video_hint: Corrections in conversation; بالعكس with a head shake.

vocabulary.teaching_note: ق is g: maʿguul. سعر معقول 'a reasonable price'; as a question معقول؟ means 'is that even possible?'. مش معقول 'unbelievable'.
vocabulary.image_scene: A shopkeeper and customer nodding over a price tag.

example.english: The price is reasonable, in my opinion

vocabulary.video_hint: Bargaining or reacting; معقول as a verdict or a gasp.

dialogue.transliteration: maʿleesh, bass ana mish muwaafig. saltat ummi aḥsan

dialogue.transliteration: hahaha, haadha ṣaḥḥ, maa agdarsh aʿaariḍ
dialogue.english: Haha, that's right, I can't argue with that

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.arabic: بالعكس، أنا مبسوط إنك جرّبته. في رأيي، السعر مش معقول بس

dialogue.english: On the contrary, I'm glad you tried it. In my opinion, only the price is unreasonable

sound_spotlight.explanation: Heavy dh with the tongue pulled back, then a doubled n. If it comes out as azunn you sound Egyptian; hold the interdental.
The complementiser and the pronoun make one word with a doubled n. After a vowel the whole thing can shrink to -nnuh.
Rising tone on a doubled ḥ at the end of a sentence turns a statement into a check. It invites agreement rather than demanding it.

lesson_sequence.detail: The Abdo–Ali dialogue once; the learner marks each line as opinion, agreement or disagreement.
أظن / أحس / يعجبني / أكره on cards with the إن link highlighted; two examples each.
The six feeling words with faces; a listen-and-tap round on the face that matches the audio.
Audio snippets; the learner taps whether each opening (عندك حق بس، مع احترامي، بالعكس، بصراحة) leads to agreement or disagreement.
The AI states a light opinion (Adeni tea vs Sanaani tea); the learner agrees or disagrees with a softener and gives one reason from Lesson 2.
Three life situations on screen; the learner records أحس / أنا + feeling + إن sentence for each.
Counter; nudge to ask ايش رأيك؟ once today.

real_world_prompts.prompt: Ask a Yemeni friend ايش رأيك في…؟ about a dish and disagree once, starting with عندك حق، بس.
real_world_prompts.context: Lesson-complete screen. Activates opinion asking and softened disagreement.

real_world_prompts.prompt: Tell someone how you feel today with أنا + a feeling word + لأن.
real_world_prompts.context: Follow-up notification. Feelings plus a reason from Lesson 2.

real_world_prompts.prompt: Watch a Yemeni reaction video and note every بصراحة and في رأيي.
real_world_prompts.context: Video-companion; recognition of opinion markers in fast speech.

video_needs.scene: Two friends disagreeing lightly on food or football; a reaction video with بصراحة verdicts; a mafraj debate with softeners audible.
